why: One table, read by both halves of the app, so the two spellings of shell
quoting cannot drift apart in silence.
Rust's `cloudbox::script::quote` is the authority: it wraps every value
this app sends to a machine. The frontend keeps one small copy
(`remoteShell.ts::shQuote`) for the handful of lines the connect wizard
types into a shell that is already open — a token to export, a runner name
— and a copy that quietly stopped agreeing with the original would be a
quoting bug found on somebody's box rather than in a test.
So both read this file. Change one implementation and its own test fails
here; change the rule for real and both have to be updated together.
